records.name_note: NC State's dedicated page lists three common names, alphabetized in its page-title parenthetical (Peacock Plant, Zebra Plant, Zebra Prayer Plant) and in its rendered Common Name(s) list. Its Description opens "Zebra plant is an evergreen rhizomatous perennial". Zebra Plant is already the landed common name of Haworthiopsis attenuata, and Peacock Plant is already the landed common name of Goeppertia makoyana, so this record lands under the page's remaining listed name, Zebra Prayer Plant.
records.toxicity_detail: NC State's Goeppertia zebrina page carries no Poison block, so there is no human-scoped severity rating. Its tag list instead includes separate pet-scoped tags: non-toxic for cats and non-toxic for dogs (it also carries a non-toxic for horses tag). No symptom list, poison-part list or handling warning is given on the page.
unknowns: Only NC State (plants.ces.ncsu.edu) has a dedicated page for Goeppertia zebrina. RHS returned 404 for both goeppertia-zebrina and calathea-zebrina, and its search page showed no entry. MoBot, Clemson and UF/IFAS could not be loaded or had no dedicated page, so every field rests on one source and nothing is cross-checked.

toxic_to_pets=false rests on NC State's separate 'non-toxic for cats' and 'non-toxic for dogs' tags only. The page has no Poison block, so there is no symptom list or human-scoped rating, and no second admissible source confirms it.

chill_damage_f left null: the page says to bring the plant inside 'before temperatures drop below 60 degrees Fahrenheit' when it is outdoors in summer. That is a precaution, not a stated damage-onset temperature.
day_f and night_f left null: the page gives one consistent range of 65 to 75 degrees Fahrenheit, not a day/night split.
humidity_pct_max left null: the page only says 'above 60%'.

light_fc_min and light_fc_good left null: prose says 'bright, indirect light or partial shade' with no foot-candle figure. direct_sun_hours_max left null because the only hour figure is the site-wide light-category legend; species prose says only that direct sunlight can scorch the leaves.

outdoor_sun_exposure part_shade comes from NC State's structured Light field 'Partial Shade'. Other sources could not be checked. USDA zones 10a-11b are listed, so it is only an outdoor plant in frost-free climates.
soil_base: the page names 'peat-based potting mix or African violet potting mix'. standard_potting was chosen for the peat-based mix; african_violet is an equally valid reading.
soil_drainage moderate comes from 'moist, well-drained' plus the Good Drainage and Moist pair. 'Overwatering can cause root rot' and 'avoid overwatering or soggy soils' rule out moisture_retentive.

water_regime keep_moist comes from the watering prose 'The soil needs to be moist, but avoid overwatering or soggy soils'. Dry-down depth and interval days are not given; water_dry_down_target, water_check_depth_cm, water_growing_days_est, water_dormant_days_est and water_estimate_basis are null.
soil_ph_min and soil_ph_max left null: NC State's pH bands are Acid (<6.0) and Neutral (6.0-8.0). Acid is open-ended and no RHS pH field was available to check the top of the Neutral band.

fertilize_interval_days, fertilize_active_months and fertilize_strength left null: the page says only 'Fertilize the plant monthly during its growing season with a balanced liquid fertilizer'. That is a word-based cadence with no stated number, no month list and no dilution fraction.
is_edible and attracts_pollinators left null: the page does not address eating or pollinators. The flowers are described as inconspicuous and the plant rarely blooms as a houseplant.
The page's Plant Type field lists Houseplant and Perennial. Its tag list also includes 'shrub', which conflicts with the herbaceous perennial habit in the Description and was not used.

records.name_note: Admissible sources split on the accepted binomial. NC State's dedicated page is titled Cissus alata and lists Cissus alata and Rhoicissus rhombifolia, and Cissus rhombifolia, under "Previously known as". RHS has no Cissus alata page that could be loaded; its page for Cissus rhombifolia leads with the common name "Venezuela treebine" and lists "grape ivy" under Other common names. Grape Ivy is kept as common_name because NC State's Description opens with Grape Ivy and its rendered Common Name(s) list, which is alphabetized, also starts with Grape Ivy; the RHS page is for a different binomial, so it was not used for care data. Missouri Botanical Garden could not be loaded.
records.toxicity_detail: NC State's Cissus alata page has no Poison block. Its only toxicity evidence is the Tags line, which reads in full: "#houseplant #interiorscape #hanging baskets #spreading #showy leaves #fantz #groundcover #non-toxic for cats #non-toxic for horses #non-toxic for dogs #partial shade tolerant #container plant #vine #trellis". The page therefore states non-toxic for cats and for dogs (and horses) only as tags; no symptom list, poison parts or handling warning is given, and no other admissible source naming this species was available. Its Plant Type field is Houseplant and Vine.
unknowns: Missouri Botanical Garden Plant Finder page for Cissus alata could not be loaded (ConnectError on both www.missouribotanicalgarden.org and plantfinder.mobot.org), so no MoBot data was used.
RHS has a page only under Cissus rhombifolia (Name Status Correct), a different binomial from NC State's Cissus alata, so its sun, moisture and size data were not borrowed for this record.

water_regime left null: the same NC State page says 'Allow this plant to dry out between each watering' and also 'Apply consistent moisture from spring to fall, but reduce watering in winter' and 'prefers moist soil'. No numeric interval is given, so the water day estimates, dry-down target and check depth are null.
humidity_need left null: NC State says only that the plant is 'tolerant of low relative humidity', which is a tolerance rather than a stated need; no percentages are given.

Temperature fields and chill_damage_f left null: NC State says 'average to cool indoor temperatures' and 'Do not allow indoor temperatures below 50 degrees F' but gives no day/night ranges or damage-onset figure.
Light: NC State says 'bright, indirect light' for indoors but no foot-candle values; direct_sun_hours_max is null because the 2-6 hours figure is the site-wide Partial Shade legend text.
Fertilizer: NC State says fertilize 4 times a year during the growing season, which is not a literal day interval, and gives no months or strength, so those fields are null.

outdoor_sun_exposure part_shade comes from NC State's structured Light field, which renders exactly two values, 'Dappled Sunlight (Shade through upper canopy all day)' and 'Partial Shade (Direct sunlight only part of the day, 2-6 hours)', and from its '#partial shade tolerant' tag; this is a tropical vine that NC State lists for USDA zones 10a-12b only.
Toxicity: only NC State's non-toxic tags for cats, horses and dogs were found; there is no Poison block on the page, so no symptom or poison-part data exists.

Size: NC State Dimensions block is Height 4-10 ft and Width 3-6 ft; its description frames 10 ft as the length of a climbing vine outdoors, so height is a climbing/trailing length rather than a free-standing height.
pH, edibility, pollinator attraction: no admissible-source statement found, left null.

records.name_note: Sources differ on the primary common name. RHS's dedicated page for this taxon leads with "red edge peperomia" (the common name shown under its RHS Plant Profile heading); its Other common names entry, "baby rubber plant", is not used because it is this catalog's name for Peperomia obtusifolia. NC State's Common Name(s) list for this taxon begins with "Jelly Plant" and also contains "Red Edge Peperomia" and "Red Edged Peperomia"; I chose Red Edge Peperomia because it is the name RHS leads with and it also appears in NC State's list. NC State lists Peperomia obtusifolia var. clusiifolia under Previously known as, and lists 'Jelly' as a cultivar of this species, so it is kept separate from the landed Peperomia obtusifolia.
records.toxicity_detail: NC State's page for Peperomia clusiifolia has no Poison block and no poison-part list; its pet statement is only in the Tags list, which reads in full: "#non-toxic for cats #non-toxic for horses #non-toxic for dogs #interesting leaves #partial shade tolerant #container plant #houseplant #early care #low maintenance #interiorscape". The description also calls the plant "pet-friendly". Only NC State addresses toxicity on an admissible page for this exact name; RHS has no toxicity statement. No symptoms, handling warnings or severity rating are given.
unknowns: Only two admissible pages exist for this exact name: NC State and RHS. No MoBot, UF/IFAS, Clemson, Penn State, UMD or UGA page for Peperomia clusiifolia was found; the Clemson peperomia factsheet and the UGA container-gardening bulletin are genus-level or multi-species and were not used.
chill_damage_f null: NC State gives USDA zones 10a-12b and RHS gives H2, which are hardiness ratings, not a damage-onset temperature. No temperature, humidity or light-intensity figures were found.

direct_sun_hours_max null: the '2-6 hours' in NC State's Partial Shade light tag is the site-wide light-category legend, not species prose; the species prose says only 'bright, indirect sunlight' and tolerates low light.

outdoor_sun_exposure: NC State's structured Light field values Dappled Sunlight and Partial Shade both map to part_shade, and RHS's Cultivation text says 'Tolerant indoor plant, preferring partial shade.'; no brighter value is supported. NC State's Soil Texture (Loam, Sand) and tags are not used for soil_base.

soil_base null: the sources say 'Moist, well-drained, loamy soil' and give no potting-mix recipe or sharp/sandy requirement, so no enum token is supported. soil_drainage is moderate (moist but well-drained); it is not set to fast because no source calls for sharp or sandy drainage with no wet tolerance, even though NC State calls the plant succulent.
soil_ph_min/max null: NC State lists Acid (<6.0), Neutral (6.0-8.0) and Alkaline (>8.0) and RHS lists acid or alkaline or neutral, so no closed bounds exist.

water_regime and all water_* fields null: sources say only 'avoid overwatering' and that overwatering can cause root rot, with no dry-down or interval statement. RHS's Moisture field reads 'Moist but well-drained or Well-drained'.

Size: NC State gives 6-12 in height and width. RHS gives Max Height and Max Spread of 0.1-0.5 metres (3.9-19.7 in) with time to maturity 5-10 years; NC State was used as the anchor and the RHS figure is a wider range.
Fertilizer, edibility and pollinator attraction: no admissible source for this exact name addresses them, so they are null.
toxic_to_pets=false rests on a single source's tags (NC State); RHS is silent. The NC State page has no Poison block, so there is no human-scoped severity rating.
RHS also shows an 'Other common names' entry which was not used as a name for this record.

records.toxicity_detail: NC State's Pilea cadierei page has no Poison block and no symptom list. Its Tags line reads "#houseplant #poisonous #colorful #potted #evergreen #showy leaves #non-toxic for cats #non-toxic for horses #non-toxic for dogs #tropical feel #variegated #terrarium". The cat and dog scoping comes only from the "#non-toxic for cats" and "#non-toxic for dogs" tags. The same line also carries an unscoped "#poisonous" tag that names no animal or plant part, so the page is internally mixed. No other admissible source retrieved addresses toxicity. toxic_to_pets=false rests on the explicit cat/dog tags only.
unknowns: MoBot Plant Finder page for Pilea cadierei (taxonid=287430) would not load (ConnectError on repeated attempts), so MoBot was not used for any field.

toxic_to_pets=false rests only on NC State's #non-toxic for cats / #non-toxic for dogs tags; the same tag line also has an unscoped #poisonous tag, and no admissible source gives a poison part list or symptoms. Treat as lower confidence.

water_regime left null: NC State says only 'Water moderately in the growing season, and reduce watering in fall to late winter', which does not map to an enum token; UF/IFAS says only 'Provide for irrigation in dry weather' for landscape use; NC State's Moist soil-drainage value and RHS's 'Moist but well–drained' are soil descriptors, not watering statements. Watering interval estimates left null.
soil_ph left null: NC State lists Acid (<6.0), Neutral (6.0-8.0) and Alkaline (>8.0) bands, which are open-ended, and RHS lists acid, alkaline or neutral, so no ceiling or floor can be set.

soil_base standard_potting is read from NC State's 'peaty soil-based potting mix' only; no source gives a more specific mix. soil_drainage moderate comes from NC State's Good Drainage + Moist pair and RHS 'Moist but well-drained'; NC State and RHS agree and NC State warns that poor drainage causes root rot.

outdoor_sun_exposure: indoor-plant light advice (NC State prose: bright indirect light, avoiding full sun) is not a structured outdoor exposure, so it was not used; values come from NC State's Dappled Sunlight (part_shade) and Deep shade (full_shade) tags, RHS Full shade/Partial shade, and UF 'plant grows in the shade'.

direct_sun_hours_max, light_fc, temperature, chill damage, and humidity percentages: no admissible source gives species-specific figures. UF/IFAS zones 10 through 11 and NC State zones 11a-12b are hardiness ratings, not damage-onset temperatures.
Fertilizer: UF/IFAS only says 'fertilize regularly' for landscape ground-cover use, with no interval, months or strength; left null. No source addresses edibility or pollinator attraction.

Mature size: NC State Dimensions are Height 9-12 in and Width 6-9 in. RHS gives Max Height and Max Spread 0.1-0.5 metres (3.9-19.7 in) and UF/IFAS gives height 0.5 to 1 feet; these are broader or consistent, NC State used as anchor.
NC State's tag line says #poisonous and #non-toxic for cats/dogs together; NC State also lists Peperomia argyraea as 'often confused with' this species.

NC State's Common Name(s) list is alphabetized and its page-title parenthetical reads "Necklace Vine, Pagoda Plant, Stacked Crassula, String of Buttons", so Necklace Vine comes first only because of alphabetical order. String of Buttons was chosen as the name that RHS leads with and NC State's prose uses. MoBot has no page for this taxon.
records.toxicity_detail: One admissible source (NC State Plant Toolbox, Crassula perforata) addresses toxicity; RHS is silent, and no second source was found to check the toxic principle. NC State's "Poisonous to Humans" block (human-scoped heading) reads: Poison Severity: Low; Poison Symptoms: "Ingestion by pets or humans can cause gastrointestinal pain, drooling, difficulty swallowing, and difficulty speaking. The sap can cause skin irritation, rash, itching, and burning."; Poison Toxic Principle: Pyrrolizidine alkaloids; Causes Contact Dermatitis: Yes; Poison Part: Sap/Juice. The "Problems" tags are separate from that block and list Contact Dermatitis, Poisonous to Humans, Problem for Cats, Problem for Children, Problem for Dogs and Problem for Horses. NC State's description says: "Keep this plant out of reach of children or pets due to toxicity if ingested. Wear protective gloves when handling this plant due to the risk of skin irritation from the sap." Its problems paragraph says: "If ingested, the string of buttons is toxic to cats, dogs, horses, and humans. The sap can cause contact dermatitis."
records.water_dry_down_target: Water well, then do not re-water until the soil is dry (soak-and-dry method).
unknowns: Only two admissible sources have a dedicated page for Crassula perforata: NC State and RHS. MoBot, Clemson, UF/IFAS, Penn State, Maryland and UGA had no dedicated page that could be found.

The toxic principle (pyrrolizidine alkaloids) comes from NC State alone. RHS does not mention toxicity, so no second admissible source checks it. It is unusual for Crassula and should be treated as unconfirmed.

NC State's Poison block is headed 'Poisonous to Humans' and rated Low severity. Its Problem for Cats and Problem for Dogs tags and its prose naming cats and dogs are separate from that block. NC State's symptom sentence also says 'pets or humans'.
is_edible is false only because NC State says the plant is toxic if ingested. No source discusses it as a food.

chill_damage_f is null. No admissible source gives a damage-onset temperature. NC State says only 'It is not frost-tolerant and needs to be brought indoors before temperatures drop to 32 degrees Fahrenheit.', which is a protective bring-indoors threshold. NC State's USDA zones (9a, 9b, 10a, 10b, 11a, 11b, 12a, 12b) and RHS's H2 rating (legend: tolerant of low temperatures, but not surviving being frozen, 1 to 5 C) are hardiness ratings, not onset figures.

RHS's Max Height and Max Spread fields each read '0.1-0.5 metres' (about 3.9-19.7 in). That is smaller than NC State's Dimensions block ('Height: 1 ft. 0 in. - 2 ft. 0 in.', 'Width: 2 ft. 0 in. - 3 ft. 0 in.') and its prose 'It grows 1 to 2 feet tall and 2 to 3 feet wide.' NC State's species-specific Dimensions block was used.

outdoor_sun_exposure is full_sun only. NC State's Light field ('Full sun (6 or more hours of direct sunlight a day)') and RHS's Position ('Full sun') both support it. part_shade was not added. It rests only on NC State's second Light value ('Partial Shade (Direct sunlight only part of the day, 2-6 hours)') and its prose 'This plant prefers full sun to partial shade but needs protection in hot climates from the midday sun.', and RHS's structured Position lists Full sun only. NC State also warns 'Sunburn of the leaves can occur from too much direct sunlight.', so give midday shelter in hot climates.
soil_drainage is fast based on NC State's sand-and-loam, cactus-mix, Good Drainage and Occasionally Dry wording plus its overwatering and root-rot warning. NC State gives no wet-soil tolerance.
soil_ph_min and soil_ph_max are null. NC State lists the acid, neutral and alkaline bands (open-ended at both ends), and RHS lists acid, alkaline or neutral.

Fertilizing: no admissible source gives a species-specific feeding schedule. RHS's Cultivation line 'Apply a balanced liquid fertiliser 2 or 3 times in the growing season' is shared verbatim with other RHS Crassula profiles, such as C. muscosa, so it is genus-level text. It gives no day interval, months or dilution anyway, so all three fertilize fields are null.

water_growing_days_est and water_dormant_days_est are null. NC State gives only the soak-and-dry rule ('Water this plant well and then do not re-water until the soil is dry.'). RHS's 'Water moderately when in growth, very sparingly when dormant.' is shared Crassula Cultivation text, not species-specific, and has no numbers.
Humidity, indoor temperature ranges and light in foot-candles are not stated by any admissible source, so those fields are null.
direct_sun_hours_max is null because NC State's hour ranges are the site-wide light-category legend, not species prose.

records.toxicity_detail: NC State (plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/curio-repens) says "This plant has low severity poison characteristics." Its "Poisonous to Humans" block (human-scoped) gives Poison Severity: Low. Poison Symptoms: "Toxic if ingested by humans, pets, or livestock: loss of appetite, nausea and vomiting. If large amounts are ingested, it can cause irreversible liver disease." Poison Toxic Principle: Pyrrolizidine alkaloids. Causes Contact Dermatitis: No. Poison Part (full list as rendered): Flowers, Fruits, Leaves, Roots, Sap/Juice, Seeds, Stems. The separate "Problems" field lists Poisonous to Humans, Problem for Cats, Problem for Children, Problem for Dogs and Problem for Horses. These cat and dog tags, not the human-scoped block, are what support toxic_to_pets. The page's tags also include #poisonous if ingested and #problem for cattle, which the Problems field does not list. The page's Plant Type field lists Herbaceous Perennial, Houseplant and Succulent. The description adds: "Be aware that the plant is toxic and should be kept out of the reach of children and pets." Only NC State among the sources I could load addresses toxicity.
records.water_dry_down_target: allow the soil or potting medium to dry out between waterings
unknowns: Only NC State and RHS were loadable. Missouri Botanical Garden and UF/IFAS pages could not be fetched from this sandbox, and Clemson, Penn State, UMD and UGA were not found for this taxon. RHS's Curio repens page has no size, care, light, soil, hardiness or pollinator fields, so everything except names rests on NC State alone.

The warning about confusion with Curio talinoides subsp. mandraliscae is not stated by NC State or RHS, so it is not in name_note. NC State mentions C. talinoides only as a parent of the cultivar 'Trident Blue' (C. repens x C. talinoides).
chill_damage_f is null. NC State gives USDA zones 9b to 12 and says the plant is intolerant to frost or freezing temperatures, but that is a hardiness rating with no damage-onset temperature.

Temperature ranges, humidity, light in foot-candles, direct_sun_hours_max, fertilizer fields, watering-day estimates, check depth and pollinator attraction have no admissible-source support and are null.

soil_ph_min and soil_ph_max are null. NC State lists Acid (<6.0) and Neutral (6.0-8.0), and the open-ended acid band gives no floor. The 8.0 ceiling of the Neutral band could not be checked against an RHS pH field because RHS has none for this page.

soil_drainage fast is a judgement. NC State lists Soil Texture Sand, a bare Good Drainage tag, a coarse sand or perlite requirement outdoors, intolerance of overwatering, and root rot from poor drainage. It never says the plant tolerates wet soil.

water_regime dry_thoroughly_between is a judgement. NC State says only to let the soil or potting medium dry out between waterings, with no depth or degree, so dry_surface_between is the nearest alternative. No watering interval is stated.

outdoor_sun_exposure comes from NC State's structured Light field. Its 'Partial Shade' entry (direct sun only 2-6 hours) is mapped to part_shade. The description also says the plant takes full sun to partial shade, with partial shade better tolerated in intense heat.
is_edible is false because NC State states the plant is toxic if ingested and tags it #poisonous if ingested. No source describes any edible use.

records.toxicity_detail: All from NC State's Callisia repens page. Under its "Poisonous to Humans:" block (human-scoped): Poison Severity: Medium (the page also states "This plant has medium severity poison characteristics."). Poison Symptoms: "If ingested, the plant can cause nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, loss of appetite, throat swelling, and difficulty breathing or swallowing for children and pets. The leaves have an oil that can cause skin and oral irritation." Poison Toxic Principle: Calcium oxalate crystals. Causes Contact Dermatitis: Yes. Poison Part: Flowers, Leaves, Sap/Juice, Stems (all four listed). Handling warning: leaf oil can irritate skin and mouth; the Description adds "The sap may also cause skin irritation for humans and pets." The page's separate Problems field lists: Contact Dermatitis, Poisonous to Humans, Problem for Cats, Problem for Children, Problem for Dogs (the Problem for Cats and Problem for Dogs tags are what scope toxic_to_pets to cats and dogs; the Description's "toxic to pets and children, if ingested" names no animal). Tag line also carries #poisonous, #problem for children, #contact dermatitis, #problem for cats, #problem for dogs. Plant Type on the page: Ground Cover, Houseplant, Native Plant, Perennial, Succulent, Vine. No admissible source disagreed on scope; no edibility information given.
unknowns: Only NC State's dedicated Callisia repens page was usable. RHS has no page at its callisia-repens URL (404), Clemson returned 403, and MoBot, UF/IFAS EDIS and ask.IFAS were unreachable or had no dedicated page via the sandbox; no other admissible source was confirmed, so every populated field rests on NC State alone.

Temperatures: NC State says plants 'prefer temperatures between 60 to 80 degrees Fahrenheit' and are intolerant to frost, but does not split day from night and states no damage-onset figure, so day_f_min/max, night_f_min/max and chill_damage_f are null.

Watering: NC State gives only a soil adjective (moist, sandy, well-drained) and 'Overwatering can cause root rot or fungal diseases', not a watering statement, so water_regime and all water fields are null.

Light: NC State's structured Light field reads 'Partial Shade (Direct sunlight only part of the day, 2-6 hours)', which is the site-wide category legend, so direct_sun_hours_max is null; the prose 'prefers bright, indirect sunlight' gives no footcandle figure, so light_fc fields are null. outdoor_sun_exposure part_shade comes from the structured 'Partial Shade' field.

soil_base standard_potting is read from the NC State prose 'moist, sandy, well-drained soil or potting mix containing perlite'; soil_drainage moderate reads the structured 'Good Drainage' plus that 'moist ... well-drained' prose. The structured Soil Texture field lists Loam (Silt) and Sand.
Soil pH 5.0-6.5 is NC State's prose preference; its structured band 'Acid (<6.0)' is open-ended and was not used.
Humidity: NC State lists Humidity only as a 'Resistance To Challenges' tolerance trait, not a need, so humidity fields are null.
Fertilizer: not addressed by any source reached; fertilize fields null.
Edibility not addressed by any source reached; is_edible null.
Attracts: NC State's Attracts field lists only 'Small Mammals', which is not a pollinator; attracts_pollinators null (no pollinator mention).

Inch Plant is also a listed common name for Tradescantia zebrina and was not merged; the Tradescantia callisia / Tradescantia repens / Hapalanthus repens synonyms appear under NC State's 'Previously known as:' and Callisia fragrans is a separate taxon.

NC State's Description says 'Be aware that the turtle vine is toxic to pets and children, if ingested', which names no animal; cat/dog scope comes only from the Problem for Cats and Problem for Dogs tags.

Mature size is NC State's Dimensions block (Height 0 ft. 4 in. - 0 ft. 6 in.; Width 2 ft. 0 in. - 4 ft. 0 in.) converted to inches; the Description prose differs slightly ('4 to 6 inches tall and more than 2 feet long').

normalizations: 2026-10-09: b108 (common houseplants) landed from the post-audit records. Eight species: Zebra Prayer Plant, Grape Ivy, Red Edge Peperomia, Aluminum Plant, String Of Buttons, Ghost Plant, Blue Chalksticks, Turtle Vine. Auditor-supplied corrected wording used verbatim; every substitute quote ground-truthed with qc.py and a strict consecutive-node check before it was applied. Landing decisions: Goeppertia zebrina lands as Zebra Prayer Plant, the remaining name on NC State's dedicated page, because Zebra Plant (Haworthiopsis attenuata, b6) and Peacock Plant (Goeppertia makoyana, b81) are already landed names (both confirmed by grep); Crassula perforata lands title-cased as String Of Buttons with outdoor_sun_exposure cut to full_sun (RHS Position lists Full sun only; NC State warns of leaf sunburn) and chill_damage_f null (a bring-indoors threshold is not an onset figure); Blue Chalksticks' toxicity_detail, removed on audit, restored from the research record in the workflow journal with the researcher-process sentence removed and the #poisonous if ingested / #problem for cattle tags added; bare RHS 'Correct' quotes dropped where the audit asked (Grape Ivy's label-only quote, Red Edge Peperomia, String Of Buttons, Blue Chalksticks) and relabelled CORR beside the page-title citation for Ghost Plant; <title>-only parentheticals replaced by rendered list items or prose on Grape Ivy, Red Edge Peperomia and Aluminum Plant; NC State Light/Soil Drainage values relabelled as field values, not tags.
